problem.text: A unit of blood expires after $10! = 10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdots 1$ seconds. Yasin donates a unit of blood at noon on January $1$. On what day does his unit of blood expire?

steps.title: Where to start: divide out the time units using the factors
steps.body: To turn seconds into days, divide by $60$ (to minutes), by $60$ again (to hours), and by $24$ (to days). You do not need to multiply out $10!$. Since $10!$ is a product, you can group its factors so that some groups make exactly $60$ and cancel them.

your_turn.prompt: Find two separate groups of the factors $1, 2, \dots, 10$ that each multiply to $60$.

steps.title: Convert to hours, then to days
steps.body:
Removing those two groups of $60$ turns seconds into hours. The factors left over are $2, 7, 8, 9$ (and $1$), so the number of hours is their product.
$$10! = (10 \cdot 6)\cdot(3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5)\cdot(2 \cdot 7 \cdot 8 \cdot 9)$$

your_turn.prompt: Compute $2 \cdot 7 \cdot 8 \cdot 9$, then divide by $24$ to get days.

steps.title: Count on the calendar carefully
steps.body: Adding $n$ days to noon on January $1$ lands at noon on January $1+n$. Careful: do not count January $1$ itself as day $1$ of the wait; after one full day it is January $2$, not January $1$. Since the blood is donated at noon, $42$ whole days later is also at noon, so there is no partial day to worry about.

your_turn.prompt: What date is $10$ days after noon on January $1$?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Forty-two days after January $1$ is "January $43$". January has $31$ days, so this is $43 - 31 = 12$ days into February. The blood expires at noon on February $12$. The answer is **(E)**.

wrong_choices.D: This comes from counting January $1$ as the first of the $42$ days. After one full day it is already January $2$, so $42$ days later is January $43$, which is February $12$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
